scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported label 395–476 is the conventional western-court range, so researched dateBasis historical preserves the 476 display cutoff while world-400 retains an unverified 400–500 source interval. Ravenna capital in 402; 395 two courts did not create two wholly unrelated Roman peoples. Political authority across western provinces changed unevenly. No geometry edits, exact-year Odoacer target or invented successor links.

UNESCO Ravenna site spans fifth and sixth centuries. Only fifth-century western monuments and period-appropriate attributes are used; sixth-century San Vitale, Sant’Apollinare Nuovo and Theodoric monuments are not credited to western emperors. Galla Placidia building’s conventional “mausoleum” name does not prove her burial there.

Hoxne bracelet is one wealthy Romano-British artifact within a fifth-century buried treasure. British Museum curator interprets burial amid Britain’s transition from Roman control; no specific burial motive, named wearer, universal flight or date exactly 410 is inferred. Animal identification follows catalogue qualified wording.

Sidonius Letters II.2 was a fifth-century elite Gallic letter translated in 1915; his own description is literary self-presentation, not demographic evidence. His wife’s estate, lion-head spouts, bathing rooms, servants, weaving space and hot-summer school joke are attributed to this household/circle. No claim of universal private bathing, toilet use, medical effectiveness or typical schooling. Cambridge education chapter summary supports narrowed aristocratic networks, not literacy rates.

The Honorius sample is a surviving coin weight, not a coin: British Museum object dates 395–423 and splits the obverse inscription across left/right fields. The card normalizes spacing to D N HONORIVS AVG, expands abbreviations and translates Latin, identifying the Roman alphabet as script. It does not imply universal literacy or universal ownership of gold.

Carthage 439 and its tax consequence are drawn from Cambridge The Roman West chapter extract. Aetius’s 451 coalition from Maas is not presented as all-Roman or as durable restoration. Odoacer ruled 476–493; Ostrogothic rule does not begin in 476 despite a misleading imported fall target and some secondary timelines. Julius Nepos 474–475 in Italy/died 480 complicates “last emperor” wording; the card avoids asserting a precise Dalmatian title not directly documented in the selected excerpt. 476 is a conventional political endpoint, not total cultural disappearance.

All card claims source checked pending independent review. Imported polygon and baseline card for united Roman Empire remain unchanged. Mechanical checks and local/public page inspection are publication checks, not independent historical certification.

proposedOverrides.summary: The western imperial court governed from Italy while authority elsewhere changed unevenly. Odoacer removed Romulus Augustulus in 476, but Roman communities and eastern imperial rule continued. The map’s 400 to 500 CE polygon is not a precise political lifetime.
